mainTopic: Redeemed blemished sacrificial animals (פסולי המוקדשין): the alternate reading of תזבח ואכלת, when their offspring become forbidden or holy, and the source that a קרבן's offspring and its תמורה are holy.
overview: This amud first gives a second version (איכא דאמרי) of how to read תזבח ואכלת. By that reading, one may redeem קדשים to feed them to dogs. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rule that the offspring of redeemed blemished קדשים are forbidden: the case is an animal conceived before the redemption but born after it. An animal born before the redemption is fully holy, and a ברייתא learns this from the extra words זכר and נקבה in the פסוק about שלמים. For offspring born after the redemption, רב הונא says they are shut away until they die, because they can be neither offered nor redeemed. רבי חנינא suggests dedicating them, just before the mother's redemption, for the mother's own קרבן. רבי לוי explains that this is a גזירה so people do not raise whole herds of them. רב ששת rules that they may not be dedicated for any other קרבן, learning it from בכור. A ברייתא supports him by contrasting animals whose מום came before their הקדש with animals whose הקדש came first. The amud ends as the גמרא explains what each of the ברייתא's summary lines comes to include, and that explanation finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: A second reading of 'You may slaughter and eat'
steps.stepSummary: Some say תזבח ואכלת only teaches that eating is allowed from slaughter onward. By this reading, redeeming קדשים to feed to dogs would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: 'You may slaughter and eat' means you may only eat them from the time of slaughter onward. But by this reading, one may redeem sacred animals to feed them to dogs, and so too he would hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version (איכא דאמרי) of how to learn the פסוק תזבח ואכלת. According to this version, redeeming קדשים for dog food would be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version, earlier in the סוגיא, read the word ואכלת as 'you may eat it, and not your dogs,' which forbids redeeming קדשים for dogs. This version reads the פסוק only as a timing rule: eating begins once the animal is slaughtered. Since nothing here mentions dogs, the prohibition on redeeming for dogs is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of a teaching
You may slaughter and eat (דברים 12:15)
Permission to eat
Redeem: transfer an animal's holiness onto money
Sacred, consecrated animals

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against the first version. It is simply a different way the teaching was passed down, and it leads to a different result about feeding dogs.

phrases.english: Some say:
"You may slaughter and eat"
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in דברים about blemished sacred animals that were redeemed.

phrases.english: you have no permission to eat them
except from the time of slaughter onward.
But one may redeem sacred animals
in order to feed them to dogs.
So too he would say.
phrases.notes: He means that whoever holds this reading really would allow it, since the פסוק no longer says anything about dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the earlier reading of תזבח ואכלת on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By this reading, תזבח ואכלת only sets when eating may begin, so one may redeem קדשים to feed to dogs.

steps.title: What case does the משנה mean by forbidden offspring and milk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that offspring and milk are forbidden after redemption, and asks what case it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And their offspring and their milk are forbidden after their redemption.' What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and asks what case it is talking about. This sets up the next steps, which test possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that after a blemished sacred animal is redeemed, its offspring and milk are still forbidden. The גמרא wants to know exactly when the offspring came into being, because that decides whether this rule makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offspring
Their milk
Their redemption
What is the case? (asking for the exact situation)

phrases.english: "And their offspring and their milk
phrases.notes: This is quoted from our משנה, which is talking about sacred animals that became blemished and were redeemed.

phrases.english: are forbidden after their redemption."
What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When exactly the offspring in the משנה was conceived and born relative to the redemption.

steps.title: It cannot mean an animal conceived and born after redemption
steps.stepSummary: If the offspring was both conceived and born after the redemption, it should be completely permitted, like the young of a deer.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was conceived and born after their redemption, why would it be forbidden? It is like the offspring of a gazelle or a deer!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first possible case and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After redemption the mother is treated like ordinary, non-sacred meat, which the תורה compares to צבי ואיל (deer). An animal conceived entirely after that point has no holy connection at all. So this cannot be the case the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion that is about to be rejected
Was conceived
Was born
Gazelle and deer: the תורה's model for ordinary, non-sacred meat

phrases.english: If you say that it was conceived and born
after their redemption,
why would it be forbidden?
They are the offspring of a gazelle and a deer!
phrases.notes: Once the mother is redeemed, she is treated like a deer, which is plain non-sacred meat. So her later babies should be too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a first answer to the question in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the משנה means offspring conceived and born after redemption.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Such offspring has no connection to holiness, just like the young of a deer, so there is no reason to forbid it.

steps.title: It means conceived before redemption but born after
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means an offspring conceived while the mother was still holy but born after she was redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was conceived before their redemption and born after their redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct case for the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the offspring began to form while the mother was still fully sacred, it carries a link to that holiness. That link keeps it forbidden even though it was born after the redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Before their redemption
After their redemption

phrases.english: Rather, it was conceived before their redemption
and born after their redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case rejected in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה refers to offspring conceived before the redemption and born after it.

steps.title: Offspring born before redemption is actually holy
steps.stepSummary: From the answer, the גמרא infers that an offspring born before the redemption is not just forbidden but fully sacred.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it was born before their redemption, it is even sanctified with holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the answer it just gave. If the משנה needed a case of birth after redemption, then birth before redemption must bring an even stronger status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offspring born while its mother is still sacred becomes holy itself, not just forbidden. The משנה only says 'forbidden' because it is talking about birth after the redemption. This inference sets up the next question: where do we learn that a קרבן's offspring is holy?

keyTerms.meaning: But this: introduces an inference from what was just said
They are even sanctified with holiness

phrases.english: But if born before their redemption,
they are even sanctified with holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the case set out in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offspring born before its mother's redemption is itself sacred.

steps.title: What is the source that the offspring is holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the offspring of a sacred animal is itself holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for what it just said in step 5. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 claimed that the offspring of a sacred animal is holy. A claim like that needs a basis in a פסוק, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the inference in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that the offspring of a sacred animal is holy.

steps.title: The words 'male' and 'female' include the offspring and the substitute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the extra words זכר and נקבה in the פסוק about שלמים. 'Male' includes the offspring, and 'female' includes the תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'Male' comes to include the offspring, and 'female' comes to include the substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא that reads two seemingly extra words in the פסוק about שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא ג:א) already says 'from the cattle,' which covers both males and females. So the words 'male' and 'female' are extra. The ברייתא uses them to add two things: the offspring (ולד) and the substitute animal (תמורה). Both become holy and are treated like the קרבן itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
To include: a word in the פסוק that adds a case
An animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן, which becomes holy too
Male / female

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source that a קרבן's offspring and its תמורה share its holiness. The rest of the ברייתא extends it to blemished animals, which is the case in our משנה.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"Male" comes to include the offspring,
phrases.notes: These words come from ויקרא ג:א about a שלמים offering. They are extra, because 'from the cattle' already covers both males and females.

phrases.english: and "female" comes to include the substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words זכר and נקבה in the פסוק about שלמים include the offspring and the תמורה.

steps.title: What about the offspring and substitute of blemished animals?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that the offspring and substitute of blemished animals are also included.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this for the offspring and substitute of unblemished animals. From where do I know it for the offspring and substitute of blemished animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues by asking whether its rule also covers blemished sacred animals. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about animals fit to be offered, which are unblemished. So one might think the rule only covers the young and substitutes of unblemished animals. Our משנה, however, is about blemished animals, so this question matters directly.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know: the ברייתא limits what it has proven so far
Unblemished animals
Blemished animals
From where? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: I only know this for the offspring of unblemished animals
and the substitute of unblemished animals.
The offspring of blemished animals
and the substitute of blemished animals, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the rule in step 7 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the offspring and substitute of blemished sacred animals are also holy.

steps.title: 'Whether male' and 'or female' include blemished animals too
steps.stepSummary: The extra word אם, in 'whether male' and 'or female,' includes the offspring and the substitute of blemished animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'whether male,' that includes the offspring of blemished animals. 'Or female' includes the substitute of blemished animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question using the small extra word אם before 'male' and before 'female.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra אם adds one more case. 'Whether male' adds the offspring of blemished animals, and 'or female' adds their substitute. This supports what the גמרא said in steps 4 and 5: the offspring of a blemished sacred animal carries holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says: introduces an extra word in the פסוק
If / whether: the extra word being used here

steps.whatToRemember: Even after a blemished sacred animal is redeemed, its offspring is affected by the mother's holiness. If it was born before the redemption, it is fully holy. If it was conceived before but born after, it is forbidden. The source is זכר and נקבה, along with the extra אם, in the פסוק about שלמים.

phrases.english: When it says "whether male,"
phrases.notes: The small word אם, 'whether,' is extra, so it adds another case.

phrases.english: it comes to include the offspring of blemished animals.
"Or female"
comes to include the substitute of blemished animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra אם before זכר includes the offspring of blemished animals, and the extra אם before נקבה includes their substitute.

steps.title: What happens to offspring born after the mother's redemption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what status and fate apply to offspring born after their mother was redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those offspring that are born after their mother's redemption, what will happen with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about offspring born only after their mother was redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps dealt with offspring born before the redemption, which are fully holy. Now the case changes: the mother has already been redeemed, and the offspring is born afterward. That creates a puzzle about what to do with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring, newborn animals
Redemption, exchanging a sacred animal's holiness onto money
What will be with them? What is done with them?

phrases.english: Those offspring that are after their redemption,
phrases.notes: "Their redemption" means the mother's redemption. She was redeemed while still pregnant.

phrases.english: what will be with them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתָן וְלָדוֹת שֶׁלְּאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן, מָה תְּהֵא עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from offspring born before redemption to those born after it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is done with offspring born after the mother's redemption.

steps.title: Background: the dispute about offspring born before redemption
steps.stepSummary: Before answering, the גמרא notes that offspring born before redemption are the subject of a dispute: are they holy enough to be sacrificed, or only holy enough to graze?
steps.simpleTranslation: Before their redemption, there is a dispute about them. Some say they are holy enough to be sacrificed, and some say they are holy only to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to set the background. It is not answering yet; it is showing how the earlier case was treated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For offspring born before redemption, one view says they can go on the מזבח. The other view says they are holy but must graze until they get a blemish and are then redeemed. The question about offspring born after redemption is set against this backdrop.

keyTerms.meaning: They clearly disagree
Holy enough to be offered on the מזבח
Holy only to graze until a blemish lets them be redeemed

phrases.english: Before their redemption —
they disagree about them,
there is one who says: they are holy to be sacrificed,
and there is one who says: they are holy to graze.
phrases.notes: They wander in the pasture until they get a blemish. Then they can be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Background note that sets up the answer to step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring born before redemption are disputed: holy enough to be sacrificed, or only holy enough to graze.

steps.title: רב הונא: the offspring are shut in until they die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the question, and רב הונא answers that the offspring are put into a closed chamber where they die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those born after their redemption, what is done with them? רב הונא says: one puts them into a chamber, and they die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its question, and רב הונא gives a strict answer: the animals are put into a chamber and left there until they die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a way to deal with an animal that has no proper use. Nobody actively kills it, but it is kept away so no one benefits from it, and it dies by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: One gathers them into a closed chamber
The אמורא who gives this ruling

steps.confusionAlert: The question is repeated here on purpose. The גמרא is coming back to it after the side note in step 11. It is not a new question.

phrases.english: Those after their redemption, what will be with them?
רב הונא says:
one gathers them into a chamber, and they die.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן, מָה תְּהֵא עֲלֵיהֶן? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to step 10's question and answers it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are shut in a chamber until they die.

steps.title: Why they can be neither sacrificed nor redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב הונא: they cannot be sacrificed, because their holiness comes from pushed-aside holiness, and they cannot be redeemed, because their holiness is too weak to transfer onto money.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what else can we do? Sacrifice them? They come from holiness that was pushed aside. Redeem them? Their holiness is not strong enough for redemption to take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא's harsh answer is needed: both normal options are closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's holiness was pushed aside (קדושה דחויה) by her blemish and her redemption. Offspring that get their status from that holiness are not fit for the מזבח. Their holiness is also too weak for פדיון to take effect, so nothing else can be done with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness that was pushed aside and cannot be used for the מזבח
Shall we redeem them?
They are not strong enough

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole problem that רבי חנינא will try to solve in the next steps.

phrases.english: For how should we act?
Shall we sacrifice them? —
they come from the power of pushed-aside holiness,
phrases.notes: The mother's holiness was already pushed off the מזבח by her blemish and redemption.

phrases.english: Shall we redeem them? —
they are not strong enough for their redemption to take hold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב הונא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They cannot be sacrificed (pushed-aside holiness) and cannot be redeemed (holiness too weak).

steps.title: רבי חנינא's solution from ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי חנינא, the scholars of ארץ ישראל say: close to the redemption, one dedicates the offspring to the same קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said in the West in the name of רבי חנינא: close to their redemption, one dedicates them for the same קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: A different approach is brought: there is a way to avoid the problem altogether by dedicating the offspring to the mother's קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of letting the animals die, רבי חנינא suggests giving them their own fresh holiness for the same קרבן. That way they are not stuck with weak, pushed-aside holiness. The wording will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
One dedicates them, attaching them to a קרבן
For the sake of that same קרבן

phrases.english: They said in the West in the name of רבי חנינא:
Close to their redemption
one dedicates them for the sake of that same offering.
phrases.notes: "That same offering" means whatever קרבן the mother was originally dedicated for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way around רב הונא's harsh outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dedicate the offspring for the mother's קרבן, close to the redemption.

steps.title: Can the offspring be redeemed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording 'close to their redemption,' because it suggests the offspring can be redeemed, which step 13 ruled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Close to their redemption? Does that mean they are fit for redemption?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of רבי חנינא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said these offspring cannot be redeemed. Saying 'their redemption' sounds as if the offspring themselves get redeemed, which contradicts that.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say?
Fit for redemption

phrases.english: Close to their redemption?
Is that to say that they are fit for redemption?

steps.triggerLanguage: סָמוּךְ לְפִדְיוֹנָן? לְמֵימְרָא דִּבְנֵי פְּדִיָּיה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'סמוך לפדיונן' in רבי חנינא's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It implies the offspring can be redeemed, against the ruling that they cannot.

steps.title: Correct the wording: before the mother's redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: close to the mother's redemption, one dedicates the unborn offspring for the same קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: close to their mother's redemption, one dedicates them for that same offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the wording so that it refers to the mother's redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right before the pregnant mother is redeemed, the owner dedicates the fetus for the original קרבן. The fetus then has its own full holiness and is not stuck with the weak holiness that comes from her redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (introduces a corrected reading)
Their mother's redemption

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Close to their mother's redemption
phrases.notes: At that point the offspring are still inside the mother.

phrases.english: one dedicates them for the sake of that same offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 15 by correcting the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The offspring themselves are being redeemed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dedication happens just before the mother's redemption.

steps.title: Why not just leave them as they are?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind this whole arrangement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the offspring cannot simply be left alive as they are. This sets up רבי לוי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the animals alone seems simpler than letting them die or dedicating them in advance. The גמרא wants to know why the rabbis did not allow that.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why can't these offspring just be left alive the way they are?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rulings so far.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the offspring are not simply left alive.

steps.title: רבי לוי: a rabbinic decree against raising whole flocks
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains that it is a גזירה, so that a person does not end up raising whole flocks from these animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי says: it is a decree, lest one raise flocks and flocks from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי gives the reason: if these animals were left alive, a person might breed them into large herds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each offspring would have more offspring with the same forbidden status, and a person could end up with whole herds he is not allowed to use. The risk is that he would eventually benefit from them and break an איסור, so the rabbis made a גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a problem
Flocks, herds

phrases.english: רבי לוי says:
It is a decree, lest one raise from them
flocks and flocks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יְגַדֵּל מֵהֶן עֲדָרִים עֲדָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה, so that people do not build up herds of these animals.

steps.title: רבינא: may they be dedicated to any קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב ששת whether the unborn offspring may be dedicated for any קרבן the owner wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked רב ששת: may one dedicate them for any offering he wishes?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question builds on רבי חנינא's solution: must it be the mother's קרבן, or can the owner pick any קרבן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא said 'that same קרבן.' רבינא wants to know whether that is a requirement or just an example.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him
For any offering he wants

phrases.english: רבינא asked of רב ששת:
What is the law, may one dedicate them
for any offering that he wishes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי חנינא's solution.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the offspring may be dedicated for any קרבן.

steps.title: רב ששת: no, only the mother's קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that they may not be dedicated for just any קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: one may not dedicate them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers briefly: no, the offspring cannot go to any other קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that רבי חנינא's words 'that same קרבן' are a real requirement. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not dedicate them

phrases.english: He said to him: one may not dedicate them.
phrases.notes: He means not for any other קרבן; the mother's קרבן is still fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, only for the mother's קרבן.

steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks why this is so.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks for the reason behind רב ששת's answer. This sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling needs a basis. רבינא wants to know where this limit comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from בכור
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת learns from the word 'בשעריך' that appears both here and by בכור. Just as a בכור cannot be dedicated to another קרבן, these offspring cannot either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: we learn 'in your gates' from 'in your gates' by a firstborn. Just as a firstborn cannot be dedicated for any offering one wants, as it says, 'But a firstborn that is born as a firstborn to ה׳ among animals... no man shall sanctify it,' so too these cannot be dedicated for any offering one wants.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the source: a גזירה שוה connects these animals to a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בשעריך' appears with redeemed sacred animals and also with a בכור, which links the two. A בכור already belongs to ה׳, so the פסוק says no one may dedicate it for a different קרבן. The same rule passes over to these offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns, derives (here through a גזירה שוה)
'In your gates,' the shared word that links the two topics
Firstborn animal, which is holy from birth
No man shall consecrate it

steps.whatToRemember: Offspring born after the mother's redemption: רב הונא says shut them in until they die. רבי חנינא says dedicate them just before the mother's redemption, but only for the mother's own קרבן, learned from בכור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a clear limit on רבי חנינא's solution: the fix works only for the original קרבן.

phrases.english: He said to him:
He derives "in your gates," "in your gates" from a firstborn,
phrases.notes: One "in your gates" is in דברים 12:15, about redeemed sacred animals. The other is in 15:22, about a בכור.

phrases.english: just as a firstborn, one may not dedicate it
for any offering he wishes,
as it is written: "But a firstborn that is born first to ה׳
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in ויקרא 27:26.

phrases.english: among animals, etc.,
no man shall sanctify it,"
so too these, one may not dedicate them
for any offering he wishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from בכור using the word 'בשעריך'.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב ששת: animals blemished before they were dedicated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in line with רב ששת. It opens with animals whose permanent מום came before their הקדש: after redemption they have the laws of בכורה and מתנות, shearing or working them never brings מלקות, and they never make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב ששת. If an animal already had a permanent blemish when it was dedicated, and then it was redeemed, it is treated like a regular animal. Its firstborn goes to the כהן, and it owes the כהן's gifts. Shearing it or working with it never earns lashes, whether before or after redemption. And it never makes a substitute animal holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב ששת. This step is the first part of that ברייתא, setting up the 'weak' case, where the מום came before the הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the permanent מום came first, the הקדש only took hold of the animal's money value, not its body. That is why, once redeemed, it is obligated in בכורה and מתנות like any חולין animal. Even before redemption, its body is not holy enough to forbid shearing and work with lashes, or to create a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
A permanent blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
The firstborn law: a firstborn male animal goes to the כהן
The כהן's gifts from a slaughtered animal: the foreleg, jaw and stomach
Substituting a regular animal for a holy one, which makes the new animal holy too
The punishment of lashes (מלקות)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up about which case is which. Here the מום came FIRST and the הקדש came after, so the holiness is weak. The next case (step 25) is the reverse.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with Rav Sheshet:
Sacrificial animals whose permanent blemish came before their consecration
and were redeemed are obligated in the firstborn law and in the gifts.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן
phrases.english: Whether before their redemption or after their redemption,
one who shears them or uses them for work
does not receive the forty lashes.
phrases.notes: 'The forty' is the usual name for the punishment of lashes.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן
phrases.english: Whether before their redemption or after their redemption,
they do not make a substitute holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up רב ששת's ruling from steps 20 and 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's rule that the offspring cannot be dedicated for any קרבן one wishes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that contrasts מום before הקדש with הקדש before מום.

steps.title: More rules for the first case, and its summary: like regular animals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues the first case. מעילה applies before redemption but not after. The offspring are חולין, can be redeemed even without a blemish, and can be dedicated for any קרבן. The summary: these animals are like חולין, except that they need to be valued and redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before redemption, using these animals for yourself is the sin of misusing holy property. After redemption, it isn't. Their babies are not holy. They can be redeemed even without a blemish, and the owner may dedicate them for whatever קרבן he wants. The rule: they are like regular animals in every way. The only holy thing about them is that they need to be valued and redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes describing the first, weaker case. It ends with a general rule that sums it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because only the money value was holy here, the babies carry no holiness that locks them into a specific use. That is why the owner may dedicate them to any קרבן he likes. This is the opposite of what רב ששת said about the second kind of animal, and it sets up the contrast that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מעילה, misusing הקדש for personal benefit
Their offspring
He may dedicate them (as a קרבן)
The general rule of the matter
The requirement to value the animal and redeem it with money

phrases.english: And before their redemption, one is liable for misusing them,
and after their redemption, one is not liable for misusing them.
And their offspring are not holy,
phrases.notes: He means babies born after the mother was redeemed.

phrases.english: and they may be redeemed while unblemished,
phrases.notes: He means babies born before the mother was redeemed. Normally a holy animal without a blemish can't be redeemed.

phrases.english: and one may dedicate them for any offering he wishes.
The general rule of the matter:
they are like regular animals in all their matters,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ בָּהֶם אֶלָּא מִצְוַת עִלּוּי בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: you have nothing with them except the מצוה of valuation alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and sums up the first case of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Sets up the contrast for רב ששת's rule.

steps.title: The second case: animals dedicated before they became permanently blemished
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא turns to animals whose הקדש came first (or that had only a temporary מום when they were dedicated) and later got a permanent מום and were redeemed. They are exempt from בכורה and מתנות, shearing or working them earns lashes, and they make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the animal was dedicated first, or had only a temporary blemish when it was dedicated, and later got a permanent blemish and was redeemed, then it is exempt from the firstborn law and from the gifts. Whether before or after redemption, shearing it or working with it earns lashes. And whether before or after redemption, it makes a substitute animal holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opposite, 'strong' case, where the animal's body itself became holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the הקדש took hold of the animal's body while it was still fit for the מזבח, because a temporary מום doesn't stop that. So even after redemption it keeps much of its holiness: it is free from בכורה and מתנות, and shearing or working it is forbidden with lashes. It can also make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary blemish that can heal
Their consecration came before their blemish
Exempt
One who shears or works with (a holy animal), which is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: A temporary מום at the time of dedication counts like no מום at all. Such an animal belongs in this strong case, not the first one.

phrases.english: But if their consecration came before their blemish,
or a temporary blemish came before their consecration,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר מִכָּאן נוֹלַד מוּם קָבוּעַ וְנִפְדּוּ —
phrases.english: and afterward a permanent blemish developed and they were redeemed,
they are exempt from the firstborn law and from the gifts.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן.
phrases.english: Whether before their redemption or after their redemption,

phrases.aramaic: הַגּוֹזֵז וְהָעוֹבֵד בָּהֶן סוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים,
phrases.english: one who shears them or uses them for work receives the forty lashes.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן —
phrases.english: And whether before their redemption or after their redemption,
they make a substitute holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to steps 23 and 24, point by point.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's rule about the offspring.

steps.title: The offspring stay holy and cannot be dedicated for any offering, which proves רב ששת right
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends the second case. מעילה applies only before redemption. The offspring are holy, cannot be redeemed without a blemish, and cannot be dedicated for any קרבן one wishes. The summary: these animals are like הקדש in every way, except that they may be eaten. This matches רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before redemption, using them for yourself is misusing holy property. After redemption, it isn't. Their babies are holy. They can't be redeemed while unblemished, and the owner can't dedicate them for whatever קרבן he wants. The rule: they are like holy animals in every way. The only thing redemption gives you is permission to eat them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the second case. Its line 'ואין מתפיסן לכל זבח שירצה' is the exact proof for רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said in step 20 that these offspring cannot be dedicated for just any קרבן, learning it from בשעריך by בכור. The ברייתא states the same rule outright for animals whose הקדש came before the מום. This lines up with step 24, where in the weaker case the owner may dedicate the offspring however he likes.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy, with the status of a sacred animal
Unblemished animals
Consecrated property
Permission to eat

steps.whatToRemember: Who came first decides everything. If the permanent מום came before the הקדש, the animal is basically חולין once redeemed, and its offspring may be dedicated for any קרבן. If the הקדש came first, the animal stays like הקדש except that it may be eaten, and its offspring are holy and cannot be dedicated for any קרבן one wishes. That second rule is רב ששת's ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling about the offspring is no longer just one אמורא's derivation from בשעריך. It now stands on an earlier ברייתא as well.

phrases.english: Before their redemption, one is liable for misusing them,
and after their redemption, one is not liable for misusing them.
And their offspring are holy,
and they may not be redeemed while unblemished,
and one may not dedicate them for any offering he wishes.
phrases.notes: This is the line that matches רב ששת's ruling from a few steps back.

phrases.english: The general rule of the matter:
they are like consecrated animals in all their matters,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לָךְ בָּהֶן אֶלָּא הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: and you have nothing with them except permission to eat alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second case, and its offspring rule supplies the actual support for רב ששת.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling (step 20) that the offspring cannot be dedicated for any קרבן one wishes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's clause 'ואין מתפיסן לכל זבח שירצה' in the case where the הקדש came before the מום.

steps.title: The first summary line includes slaughtering outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the summary line 'כללו של דבר' in the רישא of the ברייתא comes to include one who slaughters these animals outside the עזרה. He is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phrase 'the general rule is' in the first half comes to include one who slaughters them outside: he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the summary line at the end of the ברייתא's first case and explains what extra law it is teaching. It says the summary includes someone who slaughters these animals outside the עזרה, and that person is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the permanent מום came before the הקדש, and the summary was that these animals are 'like חולין.' Slaughtering a real קרבן outside the עזרה is the serious sin of שחוטי חוץ. Because these animals count as חולין, the summary line teaches that slaughtering them outside carries no punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The general rule of the matter.' A summary line that is understood to include extra cases.
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא.
'To include.' Used when the גמרא shows what extra case a phrase is adding.
Slaughtering a sanctified animal outside the עזרה (the sin of שחוטי חוץ).
Exempt; there is no punishment.

steps.confusionAlert: The summary does not mean these animals were never holy at all. They still need to be valued and redeemed (Step 24). The point is that for slaughtering outside, they are treated like חולין.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the summary 'like חולין' is not just a recap. It actually adds a practical law that the ברייתא's list did not spell out.

phrases.english: 'The general rule of the matter' of the first clause —
phrases.notes: This is the line from Step 24: 'these animals are like חולין, except that they need to be valued and redeemed.'

phrases.english: comes to include one who slaughters them outside, that he is exempt,
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means outside the עזרה, where slaughtering a real קרבן would be a serious sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back into the ברייתא just quoted (Steps 23-26) to explain what its summary phrase in the first case adds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals whose permanent מום came before their הקדש are like חולין, so one who slaughters them outside the עזרה is exempt.

steps.title: Setting up what the second summary line includes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the summary line 'כללו של דבר' in the סיפא and begins to explain what it adds. The explanation finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phrase 'the general rule is' in the second half comes to include...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא names the summary in the ברייתא's second case and is about to tell us what extra law it includes. The answer comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the הקדש came before the permanent מום, and the summary was that these animals are 'like הקדש in every way, except that they may be eaten.' The גמרא uses the same method as in step 27: a summary line always adds a case, so this one must add something too. The amud ends mid-sentence, and the added case is given at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא.

phrases.english: 'The general rule of the matter' of the latter clause —
phrases.notes: This is the line from Step 26: 'these animals are like הקדש in every way, except that they may be eaten.' The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same method as Step 27 to the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case the summary line in the סיפא of the ברייתא comes to include.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The summary line in the סיפא of the ברייתא, like the one in the רישא, comes to include an additional case; the case itself is given on the next amud.
